title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication
summary: Given two sparse matrices mat1 with dimensions m x k and mat2 with dimensions k x n, compute and return their product mat1 x mat2.
statement: Given two sparse matrices mat1 with dimensions m x k and mat2 with dimensions k x n, compute and return their product mat1 x mat2. Ensure the multiplication operation is feasible.
constraints: mat1 is an m×k matrix and mat2 is a k×n matrix, with 1≤m,k,n≤100 and values from -100 through 100.
Return the standard matrix product mat1×mat2. Exploit zero entries so multiplication work is concentrated on nonzero contributions.
target_time_complexity: O(mkn) worst case; proportional to nonzero contributions
hints: Each nonzero mat1[row][middle] contributes to every nonzero value in mat2[middle].
Initialize an m×n zero result and skip an entire inner row contribution whenever the left factor is zero.
For each nonzero left value, scan the matching row of mat2 and add left_value×right_value to result[row][column].
The accumulation is still standard matrix multiplication; skipping zero factors changes only the work performed, not the sum.
editorial: The product entry (i,j) sums mat1[i][t]×mat2[t][j] over the shared dimension. Reordering those sums by each nonzero left factor lets one update all affected output columns while skipping zero work. A second zero check avoids multiplying by sparse right entries. The independent oracle uses the direct three-loop row/column definition on generated matrices.

tests.explanation: The nonzero products give rows [7,0,0] and [-7,0,3].
Every entry in the left matrix is zero, so the 1×1 product is [[0]].
